thread:
elena: Quick heads-up — I spun up a short run comparing kernel_choice_ratio and batch_utilization signals during the midday traffic spike. Observed some weird anti-correlation with kv_hitrate.
raj: Can you paste the query you used? trying to reproduce locally. :eyes:
elena: Sure — PromQL snippet:```sum(rate(tokens_produced[1m])) by (kernel) / sum(batch_size) by (kernel)``` plus:```avg_over_time(kv_hitrate[5m])```
micah: hmm that first expr looks off — dividing tokens by batch_size gives tokens_per_batch not tokens/sec. maybe use `sum(rate(tokens_produced[1m])) / sum(rate(requests[1m]))` to get tokens_per_request then fold to batch.
elena: good call. I also pushed a quick dashboard patch that surfaces: batch_utilization, avg_queue_depth, tokens/sec, kv_hitrate, kernel_choice_ratio, and token_budget_violation_count. link: https://grafana.company/redwood/d/abc123/batching-overview
sophie: Minor observation: during the spike one kernel (kernel-v2-opt) had 2x lower kv_hitrate but was still selected ~40% of the time — suspect our kernel selector doesn't consider cache shape, only latency profile.
raj: That's consistent with the selector logic — it picks kernels by expected latency given seq_len and model type, not by kv cache hit probability. Should we add a kv_hitrate penalty to the scoring function?
micah: We can try a lightweight heuristic: penalize kernel score by (1 - kv_hitrate_smoothed). Eg: new_score = base_score * (1 - alpha*(1-kv_hitrate)). Alpha tuned -> 0.1..0.5. Keep it off by default, rollout via canary.
elena: I ran a pressure test with alpha=0.3 on a canary pool. Batch formation changed: avg_batch_size +6%, tokens/sec +8%, but tail latency p95 increased ~30ms for short requests. Tradeoff shown in the dashboard.
sophie: Do we have token_budget_violation_count spikes logged? That's the other symptom we care about.
elena: Yes — during the run token_budget_violation_count rose from ~3/hr to ~28/hr on canary. I think the kernel change made requests wait longer in queue hoping for larger batches and hit token budgets.
micah: That suggests queue policy needs to be aware of token budget per-request. Two options: (1) tighten max_wait_for_batch when token_budget_remaining low, or (2) allow immediate fallback to smaller kernel variant to drain.
raj: For telemetry we should add an annotation when token_budget_violation_count exceeds threshold and correlate with kernel_choice_ratio. Ask SRE dashboard to create composite panel: when both metrics high, mark incident.
elena: Filed infra ticket #INF-457, added panel prototype. Also added a tiny log line in scheduler: `SCHED_DBG token_budget_remaining=%d queue_len=%d chosen_kernel=%s` for quick triage.
sophie: Nice. Any perf regressions unrelated to kernel selection?
elena: I saw a small perf regression in microbatch formation code last week — extra memcpy introduced in refactor. Reverted in branch `microbatch/fix-memcpy-rollback`. Patch speeds up batch assembly by ~12%.
micah: Cool. Next actions: 1) raj to try kv-penalty scoring with alpha=0.2 on a dedicated canary; 2) elena to add token-aware queue policy toggle in runtime; 3) sophie & micah to author dashboard composite and alert.
raj: I'll start canary today, will post results.
elsa: ops-bot: deploy canary?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for scale group `batcher-canary-3` — build bld-20260318-231. Status: IN_PROGRESS. :rocket:
micah: Thanks — please paste canary metrics when done.
elena: Will do. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
